title: Unit-normalized derived scalar comparison for condensed tame-inertia invariants
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology, and a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. For $F=E,\Omega$, put $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ on profinite sets, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and let $C_E\to C_\Omega$ be postcomposition with the continuous inclusion [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and the unit-normalized adjunction $C_\Omega\otimes^L_{C_E}-\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction].

Let $r\geq0$, $G=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^r=H\times\mathbf Z_\ell^r$, and $H=(\prod_{q\ne p,\ell}\mathbf Z_q)^r$, where $q$ ranges over primes and $\mathbf Z_q=\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/q^n\mathbf Z$, with product profinite topologies. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space with continuous $E$-linear action $\rho$ of $G$ and finite image $Q=\rho(H)$ of order prime to $\ell$. Define $M_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E M)$ with its finite-dimensional product norm topology and extended action. Use the internal continuous action categories and ordinary derived invariants $R\Gamma_G$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants]. Let $u:R\Gamma_G(M_E)\to\operatorname{Res}R\Gamma_G(M_\Omega)$ be induced by the actual coefficient unit $M_E\to\operatorname{Res}M_\Omega$, $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, and the invariant/scalar-restriction comparison. Let $\sigma_M:C_\Omega\otimes^L_{C_E}R\Gamma_G(M_E)\to R\Gamma_G(M_\Omega)$ be its scalar-adjunction adjunct.

Then $\sigma_M$ is an isomorphism in the derived category of condensed $C_\Omega$-modules. More precisely, put $N=M^H=\operatorname{im}(|Q|^{-1}\sum_{h\in Q}h)$, choose the standard generators $\gamma_i$ of $\mathbf Z_\ell^r$, and form the Koszul complexes $K_F(M)$ with degree-$a$ term $\bigoplus_{|I|=a}C(-,F\otimes_E N)$ and differential $(dx)_J=\sum_{i\in J}(-1)^{\#\{j\in J:j<i\}}(\rho(\gamma_i)-1)x_{J\setminus\{i\}}$. Under the normalized derived isomorphisms $\kappa_F:K_F(M)\simeq R\Gamma_G(M_F)$ of [lem-sfb-tame-inertia-continuous-koszul], $\sigma_M$ is the canonical K-flat-derived tensor map whose representative in every degree is $z\otimes(x_I)_I\mapsto(zx_I)_I$. This identifies the actual adjunct, including its scalar unit, not just its source and target. The statement includes $r=0$ and $N=0$.

proof.text: Obtain the normalized Koszul Result from continuous_koszul, taking its auxiliary characteristic-p field to be ZMod p. Install its exact restriction and derived contexts.
Apply the unit-normalized derived tensor computation and the ordinary scalar tensor computation. These supply the two independent invertibility inputs on each Koszul representative.

Prove the pure-tensor formula from the ordinary adjunction inverse identity, linearity on sections and the recorded coordinate coefficient formula. Prove the derived transpose formula by applying the adjunction Hom bijection, cancelling the exact restriction comparison, using its naturality, and then the recorded derived unit identity.

Apply naturality of the derived Hom bijection to the normalized Koszul coefficient square. Its transpose is the derived tensor comparison followed by the localized ordinary tensor map and kappa_Omega. This is a composite of isomorphisms; cancel T(kappa_E) to deduce that the actual derived mate is invertible. Retain the quotient/Qh transports and the pure tensor formula in Computes.
